query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a minor addition of aluminum (around 2–3 atomic percent) to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will enable the in situ formation of a continuous, adherent alumina (Al2O3) scale during high‐temperature exposure, thereby significantly enhancing its oxygen resistance without degrading its useful mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr known for limited oxygen resistance but acceptable room-temperature ductility and high-temperature yield strength
generation.intervention: Alloy modification by adding a small amount (~2–3 at.%) of aluminum
generation.conditions: Exposure to air at 800 °C for a duration of 5 hours, with mechanical performance evaluated both at room temperature (for ductility) and at high temperature (around 1000 °C with strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1)
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a thin, continuous, and adherent Al2O3 protective oxide layer on the alloy’s surface
generation.mechanism: The minor aluminum addition will preferentially oxidize at the surface during high-temperature exposure, forming an alumina scale that acts as a diffusion barrier to oxygen. This mitigates the ingress of oxygen into the underlying material while maintaining the bulk microstructure responsible for mechanical performance.
generation.predicted_outcome: The aluminized alloy will exhibit reduced oxidation (evidenced by lower mass gain and enhanced surface oxide scale quality) compared to the untreated alloy, while retaining ductility (8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility) and yield strength (~163–530 MPa at 1000 °C) under the specified testing conditions.
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr experiences rapid oxidation leading to degradation at high temperatures, despite its favorable mechanical properties
generation.boundary: Testing and performance constraints are defined at exposure to air at 800 °C for 5 hours and must preserve the original mechanical performance parameters (room-temperature ductility and high-temperature yield strength at strain rates between 10−4 and 10−2 s−1).
generation.uncertainty: The optimal aluminum content for balancing oxidation protection with retention of mechanical properties is not precisely known, and the long-term stability of the alumina scale under cyclic or prolonged exposure conditions remains uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: (1) standard equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr and (2) equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr with ~2–3 at.% aluminum addition. Expose both sets to air at 800 °C for 5 hours. After exposure, conduct thorough surface characterization (e.g., SEM, EDX, XRD) to assess oxide scale formation and measure mass gain. Evaluate mechanical properties by tensile testing at room temperature and by high-temperature testing (at 1000 °C, strain rates 10−4–10−2 s−1).
measurements: Surface oxide scale integrity and composition (via SEM/EDX and XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aluminum-added alloy does not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in oxidation resistance (i.e., reduced mass gain and/or improved oxide scale quality) compared to the untreated alloy, or if its mechanical properties (room-temperature ductility and high-temperature yield strength) are notably degraded, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
